clue.text: Break in school meals initially is welcomed

indicators.note: is welcomed means the word is is taken in, received inside the other letters
initially means only the opening letter of the word meals is used

parts.note: first letter of meals

explanation.surface: Children fall out at lunchtime in the school canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division within a group, so a break in its unity.

clue.text: That woman disrupted a method of killing animals

parts.note: she refers to that woman
a strike that hit services disrupted them, so hit means disrupted

explanation.surface: A woman interrupts an abattoir's slaughter procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: Shehita is the Jewish ritual slaughter of animals for kosher meat.

clue.text: Bella was able to purchase alcohol for this reason?

definitions.text: Bella was able to purchase alcohol for this reason?

parts.words: Bella was able to purchase alcohol for this reason
parts.note: the reason anyone can buy a drink is that they carried proof of age; split that way, the phrase is a famous model's surname

explanation.walkthrough: Bella Hadid is an American fashion model; split her surname as HAD ID, the proof of age a bar asks for, and the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bella Hadid is a famous model, so her first name points to her surname.

clue.text: Head of Christian church stops to figure out favourable outcome

indicators.note: stops in the sense of plugging a hole, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: to suss is informal British for to work out

indicators.note: Head of means only the top letter of the word Christian is taken

parts.note: first letter of Christian
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A senior cleric halts proceedings to work out a good result.
explanation.definitionFit: Success is the achievement of an aim, so a good or favourable result.

clue.text: Scandinavian drinking good English beers

indicators.note: drinking means Lars takes the other letters inside him, as if swallowing them

parts.note: Lars is a typical Scandinavian man's name

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian man downs some good English ales.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a type of light beer, so lagers are beers of that kind.

clue.text: Clever like King, briefly Egypt's leader

parts.note: as means like
Tut is the short form of King Tutankhamun

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of Egypt

parts.note: first letter of Egypt

explanation.surface: As smart as the boy king Tutankhamun, Egypt's ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and sharp-witted, so clever in judgement.

clue.text: Man with helmet ordered cheese

indicators.note: ordered means arranged into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in a helmet asks for some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as asking for food, but it signals putting MAN and HELMET into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a Swiss cheese with large holes.

clue.text: Outspoken prophet of lust, perhaps, is genuine

indicators.note: Outspoken means the phrase is spoken out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a seer is a prophet and lust is one example of a sin, so a sin seer

explanation.surface: A frank seer who preaches about lust is truly honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' looks like a character trait but signals the sound. Lust is one of the seven deadly sins, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means honest and free of pretence, so genuine.

clue.text: Composer buys a secluded complex

indicators.note: complex as a noun is something intricate and tangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A musician purchases a private development of buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' reads as a noun, a group of buildings, but works as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy was a French Impressionist composer, known for Clair de Lune.

clue.text: Recited Communist broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard rather than seen, so its sound gives a spelling

parts.note: a Red is a Communist

explanation.surface: A Communist's speech is read out over the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: The past tense of read is pronounced like the colour red, which is the Communist.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a text aloud is to recite it, and the past tense is pronounced the same way.

clue.text: Think of characteristic sound by male animal in Germany

parts.note: an animal's or bird's call is its characteristic sound
a tom is a male cat
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the distinctive cry of a male beast in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: To call to mind is an idiom for remembering or recalling something, bringing it into one's thoughts.

clue.text: My first is in rift and also in Chris, My whole is in sift and also in this

definitions.text: My first is in rift and also in Chris, My whole is in sift and also in this

parts.words: My first is in rift and also in Chris, My whole is in sift and also in this
parts.note: the clue is itself written in the form of a traditional letter puzzle, and the word for a sieve used to sift is the same word as for such a puzzle

explanation.walkthrough: Old letter puzzles begin 'My first is in...'; R is in both rift and Chris, and the whole word also names a coarse sieve used to sift soil or grain.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue itself is an enigma or puzzle, and the same word also means a sieve for sifting.

clue.text: Part of accounting editorial is not tainted

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a newspaper's financial leader stays free from corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Untinged means not coloured or affected by anything, so unspoiled by any taint.

clue.text: Friend with title becomes fortune-teller

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Mister is a title put before a man's name

explanation.surface: A mate who gains a formal title turns into a clairvoyant.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmister is an old word for a palmist, someone who predicts the future by reading hands.

clue.text: Seaman eats fish spread

indicators.note: eats means the seaman takes the fish inside

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving at sea
a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A sailor tucks into a fish paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute spread on bread.

clue.text: House in Kent region where fertile old woman lived

indicators.note: in means house's letters go inside the region's letters

parts.note: Kent is in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A home somewhere in Kent where a prolific old lady once lived.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the nursery rhyme about an old woman who lived in a shoe and had so many children she didn't know what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, the old woman with too many children made her home in a shoe.

clue.text: Labourer returning additional heroin is dispatched

indicators.note: returning means the remaining letters are read backwards
is dispatched means the heroin letter is sent away, removed from the word

parts.note: fresh supplies are additional ones, so fresh means additional
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A worker on his way back finds extra drugs being sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H from FRESH to leave FRES, then 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf was a feudal labourer bound to work his lord's land.

clue.text: Gratuity in post is money for living expenses

indicators.note: in means the gratuity sits inside the other word

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a tip is a gratuity

explanation.surface: A tip arrives in the mail as an allowance to live on.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular payment, such as an allowance for a student or cleric to live on.

clue.text: Poor writer's describing psychiatrist's brother

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line round, so the writer's letters surround the brother

parts.note: a pen is a writer, and the possessive supplies the S: PEN'S
Niles Crane is the brother of the psychiatrist Frasier in the US sitcom Frasier

explanation.surface: A struggling author writes about the brother of a shrink.
explanation.walkthrough: In the sitcom Frasier both Frasier and his brother Niles are psychiatrists. 'Describing' here means going round, as a circle is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Penniless means having no money at all, so poor.

clue.text: Dash over to look at very renowned dancer

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to dash is to run
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Hurry over to watch a truly famous dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was a celebrated Soviet-born ballet dancer.

clue.text: Recalled desire to fondle soprano's spare tyre

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for soprano

indicators.note: Recalled means called back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: a yen is a desire
to pet is to fondle

explanation.surface: A memory of longing to caress a singer's paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: A Stepney is a dated British (and Indian) term for a spare wheel, after Stepney Street in Llanelli where they were made; 'spare tyre' slyly suggests a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stepney is a dated name for a spare wheel carried on a car.

clue.text: Sugar found in bone and lobster (occasionally)

parts.note: a rib is a bone

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of lobster is used

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of lobster

explanation.surface: Something sweet turns up in bone and, now and then, in shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribose is a simple sugar found in RNA.

clue.text: Dessert from America — I ruin it on the counter

indicators.note: on the counter, in the sense of counter as contrary, means the pieces run in reverse order

parts.note: US is America
to mar is to ruin

explanation.surface: A pudding from the States, which the cook spoils on the kitchen worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen counter is a red herring: 'counter' means against, so US I MAR IT is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge layered with mascarpone.

clue.text: Despicable individual back in water with swimmer

indicators.note: back in means the rear letter of the next word, water

parts.note: last letter of water
an otter is a swimming animal

explanation.surface: A rogue goes back into the water along with a swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter is a dated British word for a cad, a nasty or unpleasant person.

clue.text: Spot a piranha devouring large mammal

indicators.note: devouring means the words swallow the answer, which sits inside them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of spot across a into piranha

explanation.surface: Watch a piranha eating a large beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapir is a big hoofed animal with a short trunk, from South America and Asia.

clue.text: Yes, I roll up pants in a risky way

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or poor, so the letters are treated badly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to roll up their trousers, a dangerous move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers (or underwear to a British reader) being rolled up, but here it is the slang adjective meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Perilously means dangerously, in a way that involves peril or risk.

clue.text: New plugs placed in boat

indicators.note: plugs means the letter for new fills a gap inside the other word

parts.note: to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: Fresh bungs are fitted to a small vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A punt is a flat-bottomed river boat pushed along with a pole, common in Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: Intensify revolutionary requirement to include exercises

indicators.note: to include means the reversed word takes the exercises inside it
revolutionary means turned right round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a need is a requirement
PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: A radical demand to add workouts makes things more intense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a political adjective but only signals turning the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: To deepen something is to make it stronger or more intense, as a feeling deepens.

clue.text: Too tense to leave in a conspicuous manner

indicators.note: to leave means the letter for tense departs from the word

parts.note: overtly means openly, in a conspicuous manner
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone too anxious to walk out draws attention to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Overly means excessively, so it can stand in for too, as in 'overly keen'.
